raw_evidence: /mnt/project-files/evals-cache/f11-protect-unlock/ (ref/ reference outputs, captures and network logs; out/ our outputs, two HARs, Lighthouse JSON and logs; shots/; scripts/). Side-by-side captures: /mnt/project-files/comparisons/f11-protect-unlock/. Not in git.
harness: Playwright headless Chromium, 1280x632 and 390x664. Result read by polling the result frame every 25 ms (reference) and by a mutation observer (ours). Outputs read with pikepdf 10 (qpdf) and pypdfium2.

inputs.user-pw.pdf: 2,821 B, 3 pages, AES-256 R6, open password and owner password; its document info strings are stored unencrypted, sha256 0c7005b534ad4bd698ec0c3e4afd039dfe0937e2836178cc283768f3f644dca7
inputs.passwords: made up for this run; kept in the scripts under raw_evidence, not here

flow: Choosing a file uploads it at once (an upload check, then the upload, starting 0.4-0.6 s after choosing).

Protect options: open password; owner password; encryption RC4 128, AES 128 or AES 256, with AES 256 preselected, shown after a 'more options' link; seven permission checkboxes, all off at first: modify, copy, print, high-resolution print, fill forms, comment, insert/rotate/delete pages; a warning that readers may ignore permissions. Password fields show their text.

Unlock: a locked file opens a dialog asking for the owner password. The file's open password was refused there with a short 'incorrect' label; the owner password was accepted. Each try posts the password to a per-file check endpoint. Then one run button, no options.
The protect task request carries both passwords, the algorithm and the permission list as JSON.
Result opens in an overlay frame.
Stated free limits on these pages: 200 pages or 50 MB, 3 tasks an hour.

task1_protect.settings: alpha.pdf; open password and a different owner password; AES 256; print and high-resolution print allowed, the other five not; 1280 wide

task2_unlock.settings: user-pw.pdf; owner password given in the dialog; 390 wide

output_observations: Task 1: refused with no password and a wrong one (qpdf, PDFium); open password gives user rights, owner password owner rights. V5, R6, AES-256, P=-1532: print and high-res print allowed, extract, modify, annotate, forms and assembly refused, accessibility allowed. Metadata encrypted. 3 pages, text and render equal to the source. Title kept, producer and modification date replaced. +459 B.

Task 2: not encrypted, 3 pages, text and render equal to the source. Title and creation date read correctly although the source stores them unencrypted; producer and modification date replaced. -1,145 B.
